subtype: Stage 1: Unclear roles and a slight [Actor]
passage:
Team lead's note, Anjali, after Tuesday's client review.
Pritam presented the logistics dashboard today. It went well. But the credits slide listed only his name, and Joseph built the entire data pipeline behind it. The two had overlapped on this project because I never split the roles clearly; that part is on me.
I watched Joseph during the presentation. He stopped taking notes after the credits slide and looked at the window for the rest of the hour. Afterwards he said to me, 'It's fine,' in a voice that wasn't fine. When I asked Pritam, he looked genuinely startled: 'I just used last month's template. I didn't think.'
Next: talk to each of them separately this week, then write clear role notes on the project sheet.

qa.q: What did Joseph build behind the dashboard?
qa.a: Joseph built the entire data pipeline behind it.

qa.q: What does Joseph's 'It's fine,' said in a voice that wasn't fine, suggest?
qa.a: He feels overlooked and hurt at not being credited, but doesn't want to make a fuss, so he hides it.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Anjali at this stage?
qa.a: Talking with Joseph and Pritam separately and setting out roles clearly could fix the credit and stop the slight from turning into lasting resentment.

qa.q: How does Pritam seem to see the missing credit?
qa.a: He sees it as a simple oversight from reusing an old template and seems genuinely startled that it hurt.

grounding: A team lead notes how unclear roles left one man uncredited in a presentation; he feels overlooked while his colleague calls it an oversight.

subtype: Stage 1: Unclear roles and a slight [Actor]
passage:
Wednesday, 10:40 p.m.
Deepak presented the pricing model to the directors today. Our pricing model. I built half the formulas and every single test case. His slides had one name at the bottom: his. I sat in the back row, clapping with everyone else, feeling like a stranger at my own project.
Afterwards I said, as lightly as I could, 'Nice job. Missed my name, though.' He actually laughed. 'Oh no, sorry yaar, total oversight, I made the deck in a rush.' Maybe it was. Our roles on this were never really clear.
But can you really 'forget' months of someone's work?
Ma called and asked why her son sounded so flat. I said I was tired. Why does it sting so much?
- Vikas

qa.q: What did Vikas build for the pricing model?
qa.a: He built half the formulas and every single test case.

qa.q: Why did Vikas feel like a stranger at his own project?
qa.a: His months of work went unnamed while everyone clapped for Deepak, leaving him overlooked and hurt 😔.

qa.q: What could Vikas try tomorrow so this slight doesn't grow?
qa.a: He could calmly ask Deepak to add his name to the deck and suggest they write down who owns what, so credit is clear next time.

qa.q: How does Deepak seem to view what happened?
qa.a: He treats it as an honest oversight made in a rush, and his laugh suggests he hasn't noticed how much it hurt Vikas.

grounding: A young man's diary shows him feeling overlooked when a colleague on an overlapping project presents without crediting him and calls it an oversight.
